extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO personnel (examiners and intake staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for obtaining and proving a filing date at the USPTO when correspondence is mailed, faxed, hand-delivered, or submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system or Priority Mail Express®. Includes requirements for Certificates of Mailing/Transmission and for petitions under 37 CFR 1.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office Date Stamp notation for Certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: A notation should be made adjacent to the Office stamp indicating the date of receipt (“Office Date” Stamp) which notes the date stated on the Certificate. This notation should be “C of Mail”, “C of Fax” or “C of EFS-Web” followed by the date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a paper with a certificate dated November 10, 1997, would be noted next to the Office Date Stamp “(C of Mail. 11/10/97).” Place this notation so the Office record indicates the claimed mailing/transmission method and date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness when deadline falls on weekend/holiday
rubrics_metrics.description: If the period set for taking an action ends on a Saturday, Sunday, or federal holiday within the District of Columbia (37 CFR 1.7), the action will be considered timely if deposited in the U.S. mail, transmitted by facsimile, or transmitted by the USPTO patent electronic filing system and certified under 37 CFR 1.8(a) on the next succeeding day which is not a Saturday, Sunday, or a Federal holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply 37 CFR 1.7 and 1.8(a) to determine timeliness; e-filings and certified transmissions have special date treatment (see 37 CFR 1.6 and 1.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion for filing national application via Certificate of Mailing
rubrics_metrics.description: No benefit will be given to a Certificate of Mailing or Certificate of Facsimile Transmission relative to the specification and drawing or other correspondence for the purpose of obtaining an application filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New patent application specifications and drawings for establishing a filing date must be filed via the USPTO patent electronic filing system or by following 37 CFR 1.10 (Priority Mail Express®). Certificates under 37 CFR 1.8 do not establish a filing date for new national patent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of Certificates in the image file wrapper
rubrics_metrics.description: All Certificates of Mailing or Transmission filed in applications should be placed in the image file wrappers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure certificate documents are included in the application file records so the Office record contains the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of hand-delivered papers that contain Certificates
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel receiving a hand-delivered paper from other than U.S. Postal Service personnel should inspect the paper to ensure that the benefits of 37 CFR 1.8 or Priority Mail Express® benefits under 37 CFR 1.10 are not accorded in error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the paper contains a certificate of mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 or Priority Mail Express® mailing label, the words “HAND DELIVERED” should be written adjacent to the date stamp. This prevents mistakenly granting postage-based benefits for hand delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notify applicant when Certificate benefits denied (form paragraph 5.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should be notified in the next Office action when a paper containing a Certificate of Mailing has been denied the benefits under 37 CFR 1.8 or when a paper containing a Priority Mail Express® mailing label is denied benefits under 37 CFR 1.10 (use, for example, form paragraph 5.04).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 5.04 language and examiner notes explain the basis for denial. In bracketed fields, insert appropriate numbers (e.g., --8-- or --10--) as instructed in the Examiner Note.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 5.04 usage and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 5.04: The [1] filed [2] is not entitled to the benefits of 37 CFR 1. [3] since it was not deposited with the U. S. Postal Service for delivery to the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office. Therefore, the date of receipt in the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office has been used to determine the timeliness of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: use this paragraph when correspondence contains a Certificate of Mailing or requests Priority Mail Express benefits but was not actually deposited with USPS. Insert --8-- or --10-- in bracket 3 as appropriate. Use to document denial of postage-based filing date benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral for misuse of Certificates or improper 1.10 claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Misuse of a Certificate of Mailing under 37 CFR 1.8 or improperly claiming the benefit of 37 CFR 1.10 which appears to be more than a one-time, inadvertent error should be brought to the attention of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the pattern or nature of misuse suggests intentional or repeated misrepresentation, refer to OED for possible disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when an originally mailed/transmitted paper is not received (37 CFR 1.8(b)/(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.8(b) permits a party to notify the Office of a previous mailing through the USPS, or transmission by facsimile or the USPTO patent electronic filing system, when a reasonable amount of time has elapsed and the correspondence was not received by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may notify the Office and supply a duplicate copy of the correspondence and a statement attesting on personal knowledge (or to the Director's satisfaction) to the previous timely mailing/transmission. If the person signing did not sign the original certificate, explain how they have firsthand knowledge. Applicants are encouraged to check the USPTO patent electronic filing system before notifying the Office. In the Technology Centers (TCs), such submissions should be forwarded to the Office of Petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile and electronic filing date stamping rules (37 CFR 1.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence transmitted by facsimile to the USPTO will be stamped with the date on which the complete transmission is received unless that date is a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday (in which case stamp the next succeeding non-holiday day). Correspondence submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system will be accorded a receipt date equal to the Eastern Time when received, regardless of weekends/holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply these rules when computing deadlines; facsimile transmissions get Office receipt date treatment subject to weekend/holiday shift; e-filings get timestamp at receipt in Eastern Time even on weekends/holidays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express® filings are filed as of USPS deposit date (37 CFR 1.10(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Any correspondence delivered by the Priority Mail Express® Post Office to Addressee service of the USPS will be considered filed with the USPTO on the date of deposit with the USPS, shown by the “date accepted” on the Priority Mail Express® label or other official USPS notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the USPS deposit date cannot be determined, the Office will accord the USPTO receipt date as the filing date (see 37 CFR 1.6(a)). The “date accepted” must be entered by USPS, not by the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct deposit with USPS employee recommended; drop boxes are risky (37 CFR 1.10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence should be deposited directly with an employee of the USPS to ensure receipt of a legible Priority Mail Express® mailing label with the “date accepted”. Persons using drop boxes do so at the risk of not receiving a copy of the mailing label with the desired date accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to obtain a legible label may be considered an omission avoidable by due care. Parties using drop boxes should maintain contemporaneous records to mitigate risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express® mailing label number placement requirement and guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: While 37 CFR 1.10(b) does not require placement of the Priority Mail Express® mailing label number on the correspondence, it is advisable to do so. To be effective, the number must be placed on each separate paper and each fee transmittal either directly on the document or by a separate paper firmly and securely attached thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A cover or transmittal letter may itemize multiple papers. It is not necessary to place the number on each page, but omission of the number will preclude relief on petition under 37 CFR 1.10(c),(d),(e),(g),(h). The number should be placed prior to mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to include mailing label number is not waiverable
rubrics_metrics.description: Since filing under 37 CFR 1.10 without the mailing label number is an oversight avoidable by reasonable care, requests for waiver of this requirement will not be granted on petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law supports refusal to waive (e.g., Honigsbaum v. Lehman). A party’s inadvertent failure to comply is not an extraordinary situation warranting waiver under 37 CFR 1.183, 2.146(a)(5) or 2.148.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain contemporaneous log/book evidence for PM Express deposits
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties who use drop boxes or otherwise risk illegible mailing labels can protect themselves by routinely maintaining a log of Priority Mail Express® deposits entered within one business day after deposit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Log book entries should include Priority Mail Express® number; application or docket number; place, date and time of deposit; time of last scheduled pickup for that date/place; depositor’s initials or signature; and date/time of log entry. Such contemporaneous evidence may corroborate petitions under 37 CFR 1.10(d) or (e). Evidence created more than one business day after deposit or created prior to deposit is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.10(c) petition requirements for date-accepted discrepancy
rubrics_metrics.description: When there is a discrepancy between the filing date accorded by the Office and the USPS “date accepted,” a petition under 37 CFR 1.10(c) should: (A) be filed promptly after discovery; (B) include a showing that the Priority Mail Express® mailing label number was placed on each piece prior to mailing; and (C) include a true copy of the Priority Mail Express® mailing label showing the “date accepted.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit the petition promptly and include the label copy and proof the label number was on each piece prior to mailing. Follow submission practices in 37 CFR 1.10(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.10(d) petition requirements for incorrect USPS entry
rubrics_metrics.description: For petitions under 37 CFR 1.10(d) (USPS incorrectly entered or omitted the “date accepted”), the petition should: (A) be filed promptly; (B) show the mailing label number was placed on each piece prior to mailing; and (C) show the correspondence was deposited prior to the last scheduled pickup on the requested filing date. The showing must be corroborated by USPS evidence or evidence that came into being after deposit and within one business day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable corroboration includes USPS records (e.g., Corporate Account Mailing Statement) or contemporaneous log entries. Petitions supported only by evidence created prior to deposit (e.g., cover letters) or more than one business day after deposit (e.g., affidavits drafted later) will be denied. 37 CFR 1.10(d)(3) requires proof deposit was before last scheduled pickup for that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.10(e) petition requirements for correspondence never received
rubrics_metrics.description: For petitions under 37 CFR 1.10(e) where the correspondence deposited as Priority Mail Express® was never received by the Office, the petition should: (A) be filed promptly; (B) include a showing that the label number was placed on each piece prior to mailing; (C) include a true copy of the originally deposited correspondence showing the label number, any returned postcard receipt, and a copy of the mailing label showing the “date accepted”; and (D) include a statement signed by the person who deposited the documents setting forth date/time of deposit and declaring that the copies are true copies of what was mailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.10(e) applies only where the entire correspondence was lost in toto and only where mailed with sufficient postage and addressed per 37 CFR 1.1(a). If requesting a filing date other than the label “date accepted,” show deposit before the last scheduled pickup as required by 1.10(d)(3). The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions for returns/refusals/interruptions (1.10(g),(h),(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.10(g),(h),(i) provide procedures to petition when correspondence was returned by USPS due to interruption/emergency, was refused by a USPS employee due to interruption/emergency, or could not be deposited due to a designated interruption/emergency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such petitions generally require prompt filing; placement of the mailing label number on pieces prior to the attempt; inclusion of original correspondence or copies showing the label number; and a statement establishing the attempt/refusal/original deposit. The Office may require additional evidence to support the petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and statutory basis of Priority Mail Express filing date benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory authority for granting a filing date based on date of deposit for Priority Mail Express® correspondence is 35 U.S.C. 21(a); the specific rule is 37 CFR 1.10. 35 U.S.C. 21(a) is limited to correspondence deposited with USPS; 37 CFR 1.10 is limited to Priority Mail Express® Post Office to Addressee service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no similar provision or benefit for correspondence deposited in International Express Mail. Use 35 U.S.C. 21(a) and 37 CFR 1.10 when evaluating petitions and filing date claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office may require additional evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may require additional evidence to determine if the correspondence was deposited as Priority Mail Express® with USPS on the date in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide USPS corroboration, contemporaneous logs, and copies of mailing labels/returned receipts. Lack of adequate contemporaneous evidence may result in denial of the requested filing date.
